sourceCopy.name: Mann–Whitney U Test Calculator
sourceCopy.title: Mann–Whitney U Test Calculator Free | UsefulVerse
sourceCopy.description: Run a two-sided Mann–Whitney U test on independent samples. See U, p-value, ties and rank-biserial effect. Free and local.
sourceCopy.intro: Paste two independent numeric samples to compare their ranks. The tool reports both U statistics, a two-sided p-value, tie handling, method and signed rank-biserial effect.
sourceCopy.howQuestion: What does the Mann–Whitney U test compare?
sourceCopy.howAnswer: It compares the rank distributions of two independent samples. It is not automatically a test of medians unless additional distribution-shape assumptions hold.
sourceCopy.privacyAnswer: No. Ranking and the test are calculated in this browser. Sample values are not sent to a server or saved by this tool.
howTo: Enter at least two observations in each sample, separated by commas, spaces or line breaks.
Run the two-sided test and review the U statistics, p-value, method and rank-biserial effect.
Check whether the independence and interpretation assumptions fit your study.

fields.group1-higher: Sample 1 tends to have higher values
fields.group2-higher: Sample 2 tends to have higher values
fields.accuracyNote: Enter 2–500 finite numbers per sample (up to ±1,000,000,000,000). Separate with commas, semicolons, spaces or new lines; use a dot for decimal places. Samples must be independent.
fields.designNote: This page runs a two-sided test only. It uses an exact permutation distribution for tie-free samples with at most 40 observations in total; otherwise it uses a tie-corrected normal approximation with continuity correction. All-equal pooled values return p=1.
fields.formulaNote: The test compares ranks, not necessarily medians: a median interpretation also needs similarly shaped distributions. The rank-biserial effect is signed by sample order and describes pairwise rank dominance. The p-value does not measure effect importance, prove a cause, or replace a study-design review.

messages.checkInputs: Check both samples and enter enough valid values.
messages.copyUnavailable: Copy is unavailable in this browser.
messages.sampleFormat: Enter each sample as a list of numbers.
messages.valueRange: Use finite values within the stated numeric range.

additionalFaqs.question: Is Mann–Whitney the same as the Wilcoxon signed-rank test?
additionalFaqs.answer: No. Mann–Whitney (Wilcoxon rank-sum) compares two independent groups. The signed-rank test is for paired or matched observations.

additionalFaqs.question: Does Mann–Whitney always test whether medians differ?
additionalFaqs.answer: No. It tests rank distributions. Interpreting it as a median comparison requires additional assumptions, including similarly shaped distributions.

additionalFaqs.question: How does the calculator handle ties?
additionalFaqs.answer: It assigns average ranks to equal values and uses a tie-corrected normal approximation. Its exact permutation method is used only when pooled observations have no ties and the total sample size is at most 40.
